statement: If a finite system of $r$ congruences $\{ a_i\pmod{n_i} : 1\leq i\leq r\}$ (the $n_i$ are not necessarily distinct) covers $2^r$ consecutive integers then it covers all integers.
notes: This is best possible as the system $2^{i-1}\pmod{2^i}$ shows. This was proved indepedently by Selfridge and Crittenden and Vanden Eynden [CrVE70] . A simpler proof was given by Balister, Bollobás, Morris, Sahasrabudhe, and Tiba [BBMST20b] .
benchmark_provenance: Published informal statement and discussion; no external Lean proof supplied.
